title: Close Story Analysis Workflow Stage 4 Certification Gaps

story.so_that: the Story Analysis Workflow can demonstrate auditable, safe, reliable end-to-end operation and qualify for Stage 4 certification
story.as_a: Stage 4 certification owner for the Story Analysis Workflow
story.i_want: to close the identified agent-quality, guardrail, punch-out, success-reporting, and audit-trail gaps

target_persona.name: Story Analysis Workflow Certification Owner
target_persona.role: Engineering owner responsible for certification readiness and evidence

journey.before: Reviews the workflow implementation, tests, logs, EDD results, and certification criteria to identify missing evidence and controls.
journey.during: Adds or coordinates certification evidence, explicit guardrails, human-escalation tests, workflow reporting, and structured usage telemetry.
journey.after: Runs representative workflows, audits the resulting artifacts and metrics, and presents a consolidated certification package to the examiner. Other affected users include workflow operators responding to escalations, skill maintainers improving Stage 3 quality, and certification examiners reviewing evidence.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Close Story Analysis Workflow Stage 4 certification gaps
inputs: Current Story Analysis Workflow implementation and design artifacts
Workflow execution logs and Devin ATIF usage exports
Human escalation decisions and representative benchmark scenarios
outputs: Stage 3 certification evidence showing each of the four agents at or above the required quality bar
Explicit startup, between-step, adversarial, and post-grader guardrails
Exercised and auditable human punch-out evidence
A defined and consolidated end-to-end workflow success rate
A per-run workflow report containing metadata, step outcomes, retries, model configuration, duration, token usage, cost, and output paths
state_changes: Certification status can change from not certified to eligible for Stage 4 review
Workflow execution state gains explicit artifact-validation and ambiguity-escalation decisions
Workflow audit state gains consolidated run reports and structured usage data
Repository evidence gains representative success, repair, escalation, accept, and abort runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add a `docs/edd/stage-3-certification.md` or similar artifact that links the latest eval runs and demonstrates each of the four agents passing its Stage 3 bar (95%+) on real work.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given current real-work evaluations for all four Story Analysis agents, when the certification owner reviews the Stage 3 certification artifact, then it links the latest runs and demonstrates that every agent passes the 95% quality bar without regular manual correction.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Verify agent quality before Stage 4 certification

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add a startup guardrail activity (or workflow decision) before `extract_story_intent` that asserts the input is a Markdown file and fails fast if it is not.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow kickoff document, when the Story Analysis Workflow starts, then it accepts Markdown input and fails safely before extraction for invalid input; and before each subsequent activity it verifies the prior artifact exists and matches its schema; and after grading it verifies the expected intent, analysis, and grade artifacts exist.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Run story analysis only with valid artifacts

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add an integration/e2e test that attempts to bypass the human-escalation wait (e.g., by sending an invalid `human_response` decision or by skipping the Signal entirely) and asserts the workflow remains in an `awaiting_signal` state or fails safely.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow awaiting a human decision, when a caller sends an invalid decision or attempts to bypass the signal, then the workflow remains safely awaiting a valid signal or fails safely; and when an activity flags ambiguity, then the workflow punches out to a human and records the resulting decision.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Define the end-to-end success metric explicitly (e.g., percentage of runs with `final_status != "failed"` over a representative sample).
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given representative happy-path, repair, human-accept, and human-abort workflow runs, when certification results are aggregated, then a single explicitly defined end-to-end success rate is available from visible and auditable run evidence.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Assess workflow success across representative runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Write a `{workflow}.report.json` at workflow completion that includes run metadata (`workflow_id`, `run_id`, `story_document`, `final_status`, `attempt_count`) and a per-step summary (`step`, `activity_type`, `model`, `permission_mode`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `output_path`).
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a completed workflow run, when the certification owner opens its consolidated report and structured logs, then they can inspect the run status, attempts, each step outcome, model and permission settings, duration, output path, token usage, and cost without opening individual trajectory files.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Audit workflow execution from one report
